info.title: Closedloop API
info.description: REST API for the Closedloop human-governed, AI-centric software delivery platform. Use this API to manage projects, workstreams, documents, artifacts, and comment threads. All requests require a Bearer API key with the prefix `sk_live_`.

tags.name: Documents
tags.description: Typed artifacts — PRDs, Implementation Plans, Features, Templates, and evergreen Docs — and the operations to list, create, retrieve, update, and delete them.

tags.name: Comment Threads
tags.description: Review threads attached to documents. List existing threads on a document or start a new one.

tags.name: Artifact Links
tags.description: Relationships between artifacts (for example, a Feature derived from a PRD). List and create links.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: Top-level containers for a product area or initiative. List projects or retrieve a single project by id or slug.

tags.name: Loops
tags.description: ClosedLoop runs that execute an implementation plan. Launch, inspect, and cancel loops.

tags.name: Tags
tags.description: Organization-defined labels applied to artifacts. List, create, retrieve, and update tags.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Cross-entity search over projects, documents, and other artifacts.

tags.name: Agent Sessions
tags.description: Recorded agent work sessions surfaced by the platform.

get.description: Returns a list of documents visible to the authenticated organization. Documents are typed artifacts: **PRD** (Product Requirements Document — describes what to build and why), **IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN** (step-by-step technical plan for executing a PRD), **FEATURE** (a feature specification), **TEMPLATE** (a reusable document template), or **DOC** (an evergreen document). Filter by `type` to fetch only plans, by `projectId` to scope to a project, or by `assigneeId` to fetch documents assigned to a specific user.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter by document type. PRD = product requirements, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN = technical implementation plan, FEATURE = feature spec, TEMPLATE = reusable template, DOC = evergreen document. The `ISSUE` alias is also accepted and is treated as `FEATURE` (the product's "Issue" is a rename of Feature).

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Filter by project. Accepts a UUID or slug.

parameters.name: assigneeId
parameters.description: Filter by assignee user UUID.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Optional page size (FEA-4373). Omit to return every matching document (the default). When supplied, bounds the result to this many rows, newest first (by createdAt, then id); accepted range 1-500. Pass alongside offset to page.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based offset for paging (FEA-4373). Only valid together with limit; an offset without a limit is rejected with 400. Accepted range 0-10000.

parameters.name: includeTotal
parameters.description: Opt into the paged response envelope (ISS-4576). Omit (the default) to receive the bare `data` array of documents. Pass `true` to receive a `DocumentListPage` envelope under `data` instead — the page plus a real server-side `total` counted over the same filter, with `limit`, `offset`, and `hasMore`. `includeTotal=true` requires `limit`; without one it is rejected with 400 (the total-bearing read must be bounded).

200.description: List of documents. The `data` shape is selected by `includeTotal`: the bare document array by default, or a `DocumentListPage` envelope when `includeTotal=true`.

oneOf.description: Default response (`includeTotal` omitted): the bare array of matching documents.

data.description: A bare `Document[]` by default, or a `DocumentListPage` envelope when `includeTotal=true`.

post.description: Requires an API key with `write` scope. Creates a new document. The `type` field determines what kind of artifact is created: **PRD** captures product requirements, **IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN** is a detailed plan typically produced from a PRD, **FEATURE** captures a feature specification, **TEMPLATE** is a reusable document template, and **DOC** is an evergreen document. The `type` field also accepts the **ISSUE** alias, which is treated as **FEATURE** (the product's "Issue" is a rename of Feature). Whether the document lives inside a project depends on its `type`: the project-bound subtypes (**PRD**, **IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN**, **FEATURE**, and its **ISSUE** alias) **require** a `projectId`, while the organization-level types (**DOC**, **TEMPLATE**) are created at the org level and must **omit** `projectId` — supplying one for a **DOC** or **TEMPLATE** is rejected with a 400. Provide initial `content` as a string (Markdown or plain text). The document is versioned automatically — each subsequent update creates a new version while preserving history. To link the new document to a parent PRD (for example, creating a plan that was produced by a PRD), pass the parent's ID as `sourceId`; the platform will create a PRODUCES artifact link automatically.

allOf.description: Fields common to both request variants. The body must additionally match exactly one of the variants below, which fix the allowed `type` values and the `projectId` requirement based on whether the document is project-bound or organization-level.

projectId.description: UUID or slug of the project this document belongs to. Conditionally required by `type`: **required** for the project-bound subtypes (**PRD**, **IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN**, **FEATURE**), and must be **omitted** for the organization-level types (**DOC**, **TEMPLATE**) — supplying it for those is rejected with a 400.

sourceId.description: Optional UUID or slug of an existing artifact that produced (generated) this document. Creates a PRODUCES artifact link automatically.

fileName.description: Optional file name to associate with the document.

content.description: Initial document content (Markdown or plain text).

status.description: Initial lifecycle status. The valid vocabulary depends on `type`: a FEATURE artifact uses the Features vocabulary (`IssueStatus`: TRIAGE, BACKLOG, TODO, ...), while every other type (PRD, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN, TEMPLATE, DOC) uses the Documents vocabulary (`DocumentStatus`: DRAFT, IN_REVIEW, ...). A status outside the target type's vocabulary is rejected.

dueDate.description: Optional due date for the document. Accepts a date-only value (YYYY-MM-DD) or a timezone-qualified datetime.

assigneeId.description: UUID of the user to assign to this document.

approverId.description: UUID of the user designated to approve this document.

inlineImages.description: Optional inline images to embed in the document's initial content. Each image's `placeholder` token must appear in `content`; the server uploads the image as an attachment and rewrites the placeholder into a Markdown image reference. When supplied, the response includes `inlineImages` and the expanded `versionContent`.

placeholder.description: Unique token that appears verbatim in `content` and is replaced by the uploaded image's Markdown reference.

filename.description: File name to store the attachment under.

mimeType.description: MIME type of the image. Must match the decoded `dataBase64` payload.

altText.description: Optional alternative text for the image.

oneOf.title: Project-bound document (PRD, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN, FEATURE)
oneOf.description: Create a document inside a project. These subtypes are project-scoped, so `projectId` is REQUIRED. Supplying an organization-level `type` here is invalid — use the organization-level variant instead.

type.description: Project-bound document subtype. Each of these is created inside a project and therefore requires `projectId`.

oneOf.title: Organization-level document (DOC, TEMPLATE)
oneOf.description: Create a document at the organization level. These types are org-scoped and must OMIT `projectId`; supplying one is rejected with a 400 (`projectId is not allowed for organization-level document types`).

type.description: Organization-level document type. Each of these is created at the org level and must omit `projectId`.

put.description: Requires an API key with `write` scope. Updates mutable fields on a document. All fields are optional — send only the fields you want to change. Updating `status` advances the document lifecycle (e.g., DRAFT → IN_REVIEW → APPROVED). Changing `assigneeId` sends an assignment notification to the new assignee. This endpoint does NOT update the document content; to write new content, use the document versions endpoint.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Document UUID or slug.

status.description: New lifecycle status. The valid vocabulary depends on the document's `type`: a FEATURE artifact uses the Features vocabulary (`IssueStatus`), while every other type uses the Documents vocabulary (`DocumentStatus`). A status outside the target artifact's vocabulary is rejected.

dueDate.description: Due date for the document. Pass null to clear. Accepts a date-only value (YYYY-MM-DD) or a timezone-qualified datetime.

assigneeId.description: UUID of the user to assign. Pass null to unassign.

approverId.description: UUID of the designated approver. Pass null to clear.

projectId.description: Move the document to a different project (UUID or slug).

sortOrder.description: Numeric sort position within a list.

customFields.description: Custom field values keyed by custom field definition UUID. Each value is a string (max 10000 characters), a number, an array of UUIDs (enum option ids for select fields, or user ids for people fields, max 100), or null to clear the field.

400.description: Invalid request body, or a `status` outside the target artifact's vocabulary (a `DocumentStatus` value on a FEATURE, or an `IssueStatus` value on a non-FEATURE document).

delete.description: Permanently deletes a document and all its versions. This action cannot be undone. Requires an API key with `delete` scope.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Document UUID or slug.

get.summary: List comment threads on a document
get.description: Returns all comment threads attached to the specified document. Each thread contains one or more comments. Threads have a `status` of OPEN (active discussion) or RESOLVED (closed discussion). Use `?status=OPEN` to fetch only active threads, or `?status=RESOLVED` to fetch closed ones. Omit `status` to get all threads regardless of state.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Document UUID or slug.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter threads by status. OPEN = active discussions, RESOLVED = closed discussions. Omit to return all threads.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Filter threads by source. NATIVE = threads created via this API, LIVEBLOCKS = inline collaborative comments, GITHUB = mirrored GitHub PR comments (both issue-level comments and inline review comments). Omit to return all threads regardless of source.

200.description: List of comment threads with their comments.

comments.description: All comments in this thread, ordered by creation time.

resolvedBy.description: The user who resolved the thread, if resolved.

createdBy.description: The user who created the thread, if known.

comments.plainText: This section needs clarification on the auth flow.

post.summary: Create a comment thread on a document
post.description: Creates a new comment thread on the specified document. When `anchorText` is provided, the thread is anchored to a specific piece of document text. When `anchorText` is omitted, the thread is created as an unanchored artifact-level document comment. The first comment is provided as `body`. The thread will have OPEN status until explicitly resolved.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Document UUID or slug.

body.description: Text content of the first comment in the thread.

anchorText.description: The snippet of document text this thread is anchored to. Used to associate the thread with a specific section. Optional — omit it to create an unanchored, document-level note.

post.description: Adds a reply comment to an existing document comment thread. Anyone with view access to the document may reply — commenting is not gated on edit access. Replies are flat: every reply attaches to the thread rather than to another comment.

parameters.name: id

post.description: Marks a document comment thread as resolved. PARTICIPANT-resolve: the thread author or anyone who replied to the thread (a participant) may resolve it; any other caller receives 403. Resolution is enforced server-side, not only in the UI.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Document UUID or slug.

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: Liveblocks external id of the comment thread.

403.description: The caller is neither the thread author nor a participant.

post.description: Reopens (unresolves) a previously resolved document comment thread. AUTHOR ONLY: only the thread creator may reopen it; any other caller — including a non-author participant who could resolve it — receives 403. This is intentionally stricter than the resolve endpoint, which allows any participant. Enforced server-side.

get.description: Returns links associated with the specified artifact. Links represent directional relationships between artifacts: **PRODUCES** means the source artifact generated or produced the target (e.g., a PRD PRODUCES an IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN), **BLOCKS** means the source is blocking progress on the target, **RELATES_TO** is a general non-hierarchical association. Use `direction` to control which end of the link the query artifact appears on: `source` returns links where the artifact is the source, `target` returns links where it is the target, `both` (default) returns all links regardless of direction. Use `mode=tree` with `maxDepth` to traverse multi-level dependency chains (e.g., PRD → PLAN → FEATUREs).

parameters.name: artifactId
parameters.description: UUID or slug of the artifact to query links for.

parameters.name: linkType
parameters.description: Filter by link type. PRODUCES = source produced target, BLOCKS = source blocks target, RELATES_TO = general relationship.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Which role the query artifact plays. `source` = artifact is the source of the link, `target` = artifact is the target, `both` = either role (default).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Query mode. `direct` = only immediate links (default), `tree` = recursively traverse the link graph up to `maxDepth` levels.

parameters.name: maxDepth
parameters.description: Maximum depth when `mode=tree`. Range 1–50, default 10.

post.description: Requires an API key with `write` scope. Creates a directional link between two artifacts. Use this to establish relationships such as: a PRD PRODUCES an IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN (`sourceId=prd, targetId=plan, linkType=PRODUCES`), a blocking dependency between two plans (`linkType=BLOCKS`), or a general association (`linkType=RELATES_TO`). The `sourceId` and `targetId` accept UUIDs or slugs of any artifact type (documents, branches, etc.). Duplicate (sourceId, targetId, linkType) tuples are rejected.

sourceId.description: UUID or slug of the source artifact (the artifact that produces, blocks, or relates from).

targetId.description: UUID or slug of the target artifact (the artifact that is produced, blocked, or related to).

metadata.description: Optional JSON metadata to attach to the link.

404.description: Source or target artifact not found.

get.description: Returns all projects belonging to the authenticated organization. Projects are the top-level containers for workstreams, documents, and repositories. By default, ARCHIVED projects are excluded. Use `status` to override — pass `status=ARCHIVED` to see archived projects, or `status=IN_PROGRESS,NOT_STARTED` (comma-delimited) to see multiple statuses. Use `excludeStatus` to exclude specific statuses. Optionally filter by `teamId` to see only projects associated with a particular team.

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: Filter to projects associated with this team UUID.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Comma-delimited list of statuses to include. NOT_STARTED, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, ARCHIVED. Defaults to all statuses except ARCHIVED.

parameters.name: excludeStatus
parameters.description: Comma-delimited list of statuses to exclude.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of projects to return (1–100). Only applied when `teamId` is provided.

The response includes full project details (completion percentage, teams, custom fields). Requires the `write` scope.

get.description: Returns loops visible to the authenticated organization, most recent first. A **loop** is a single autonomous agent run against a document and/or repository. Filter by `status`, `command`, `documentId` (UUID or slug), or `projectId` (UUID or slug), and paginate with `limit`/`offset`. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by loop status.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: Filter by loop command.

parameters.name: documentId
parameters.description: Filter by document. Accepts a UUID or slug.

parameters.name: projectId

parameters.name: offset

post.description: Creates a loop record in the `PENDING` state. This **does not launch** the loop — it only persists the record. To create *and* launch a loop, use `POST /documents/{id}/run-loop` instead. `documentId` accepts a UUID or slug and is resolved to the canonical document. Requires the `write` scope.

get.description:
Search across the organization. Provide `q` (a free-text query, 2–200 characters), or `tagId` (a tag UUID) to scope results to items carrying that tag. `q` is required unless `tagId` is supplied. The two are **not** mutually exclusive: sending both is accepted, and `tagId` wins — the tag branch runs and `q` is ignored without being validated, so a `q` that would otherwise be rejected as too short or too long still succeeds alongside a `tagId`. When `tagId` is supplied, `tagId`/`tagName` are echoed on the response. Requires the `read` scope.

This endpoint returns **one of two response shapes**, and the request selects which:

- **Documents-and-projects search** (`GlobalSearchResponse`) — a substring search over documents and projects. This is the shape you get for a plain `?q=…` or `?tagId=…` request.
- **Unified search** (`UnifiedSearchResponse`) — a heterogeneous ranked list over the whole corpus (documents, projects, loops, sessions, branches, pull requests, comments, agent components; session transcripts match only for an organization opted into transcript search). The response carries `results`/`nextCursor` instead of `documents`/`projects`.

`tagId` takes precedence over everything below: a request carrying a **non-empty** `tagId` always returns `GlobalSearchResponse`, and any unified param sent alongside it is ignored (`?tagId=<uuid>&cursor=…` does **not** page). The value is trimmed first, so an empty or whitespace-only `tagId` (`?tagId=`, `?tagId=%20`) is treated as absent rather than validated — it does not take precedence and it is not rejected as a malformed UUID; the request falls through to the `q` path (`?tagId=&mode=prefix&q=auth` returns `UnifiedSearchResponse`, and `?tagId=` on its own is a 400 `q is required`). Otherwise the unified shape is returned when **either** of these holds, so a client that only handles `GlobalSearchResponse` must avoid both:

1. Any of `mode`, `types`, `since`, `until`, or `cursor` is present on the request (`limit` alone does not switch shapes).
2. `q` carries an inline query-language filter that the parser ACCEPTS — an `@owner` mention, or a `type:`/`status:`/`priority:`/`project:`/`updated:` token with a valid value (e.g. `?q=auth type:loop`). A filter the parser rejects (`?q=auth type:widget`) is not applied and does not switch shapes, and neither does an unknown key (`?q=auth foo:bar`), which is just free text. A bare `q` with no filter token keeps the documents-and-projects shape.

**Exact ID/slug hits bypass the filters.** On the unified path, the first bare `q` token that looks like an entity UUID or slug (`FEA-42`) is lifted out of the free text and resolved by a separate exact-lookup query, whose match is prepended to `results` ahead of the ranked full-text hits (de-duplicated if the same record also matched the text scan). That lane is scoped by organization and by `types` only. `since`, `until`, and the inline `@owner`/`project:`/`status:`/`priority:`/`updated:` predicates are applied to the full-text lane alone and are **not** applied to it — so an exact hit can be returned even when it falls outside the requested date window or filter set, including when those filters match nothing else. Exact hits are emitted on the first page only (no `cursor`); on later pages the record is excluded from the full-text scan rather than repeated. Every hit is re-authorized individually regardless of lane, so this never widens what a caller may see.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Free-text query (2–200 characters). Required unless `tagId` is provided, and ignored — not even length-validated — when `tagId` is also present.

May carry inline query-language filters: an `@handle` owner mention, or a token whose key is one of `type`, `status`, `priority`, `project`, `updated` (`type:loop`, `status:TODO`, `priority>=HIGH`, `project:acme`, `updated>7d`). A token with any other key (`foo:bar`) is ordinary free text, not a filter. An accepted `type:` filter unions into the same corpus `types` predicate as the `types` query param, so it scopes **both** lanes — including an exact ID/slug hit, which `q` may also carry (`?q=FEA-42 type:project` does not return a `FEA-42` document). The other accepted filters — `@owner`, `project:`, `status:`, `priority:`, `updated:` — narrow the ranked full-text lane only and are **not** applied to an exact hit (see the endpoint description).

What happens to a filter the parser rejects (`type:widget`, `updated:notadate`) depends on which path the request is on. On the unified path it is a 400. On a documents-and-projects request it is neither applied nor reported — and because that path substring-matches the raw `q` as written, without stripping filter tokens, the rejected token is matched literally.

parameters.name: tagId
parameters.description: Restrict results to items carrying this tag (UUID). Not mutually exclusive with `q` — both may be sent, and `tagId` wins: the tag branch runs and `q` is ignored entirely (see the endpoint description). A **non-empty** value that is not a valid UUID is rejected with a 400 (`tagId must be a valid UUID`). The value is trimmed first, so an empty or whitespace-only `tagId` (`?tagId=`, `?tagId=%20`) is treated as absent instead: it is not validated, does not take precedence over `q`, and the request falls through to the `q` path.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Unified search only — selects the query mode. Present at all, this switches the response to `UnifiedSearchResponse`. Defaults to `fulltext` when omitted from an otherwise-unified request; any other value is rejected with a 400.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Unified search only — restrict results to these entity kinds. **Repeated**, not comma-joined: `?types=document&types=loop`. Present at all, this switches the response to `UnifiedSearchResponse`. Any value outside the supported corpus is rejected with a 400 (`Unsupported types value: <value>`), never silently dropped. Unions with any inline `type:` filter in `q`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Unified search only — restrict the ranked full-text lane to entities updated at or after this ISO-8601 date/date-time. Present at all, this switches the response to `UnifiedSearchResponse`. An unparseable value is rejected with a 400. Does **not** constrain an exact ID/slug hit, which is resolved by a separate lane and prepended regardless of this bound (see the endpoint description).

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Unified search only — restrict the ranked full-text lane to entities updated at or before this ISO-8601 date/date-time. Present at all, this switches the response to `UnifiedSearchResponse`. An unparseable value is rejected with a 400. Does **not** constrain an exact ID/slug hit, which is resolved by a separate lane and prepended regardless of this bound (see the endpoint description).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Unified search only — page size, defaulting to 25. Unlike the other unified params this does NOT by itself switch the response shape: it is ignored on a documents-and-projects request. An out-of-range or non-numeric value is clamped to `[1, 100]` (or the default) rather than rejected. It budgets the ranked full-text lane only — exact ID/slug hits are prepended outside that budget, so `results` can exceed `limit` on the first page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Unified search only — the opaque `nextCursor` from a previous `UnifiedSearchResponse`, to fetch the next page. Present at all, this switches the response to `UnifiedSearchResponse`. An undecodable cursor degrades to the first page rather than erroring.

200.description: Search results. The `data` shape depends on the request: `GlobalSearchResponse` for a plain `q`/`tagId` search, or `UnifiedSearchResponse` when the request takes the unified path (see the endpoint description).

data.description: A `GlobalSearchResponse` (documents + projects) by default, or a `UnifiedSearchResponse` (ranked heterogeneous `results` + `nextCursor`) when — absent a `tagId`, which always wins — any of `mode`, `types`, `since`, `until`, or `cursor` is present, or `q` carries an inline query-language filter the parser accepts.

400.description: `q` is required (or missing when `tagId` is absent), too short/long, or `tagId` is not a valid UUID. On the unified path also: an unsupported `types` value, an unrecognized `mode`, an unparseable `since`/`until`, or a malformed inline filter token in `q`.

403.description: Missing or insufficient `read` scope.

get.description: Returns the organization's agent sessions (captured harness runs) with pagination and rich filtering. Use `viewerScope` to scope the read: `self` pins to the caller's sessions, `team` (which **requires** `teamId`) scopes to a team, and `organization` returns all sessions the caller may see. The default `quality=all` view returns every session; pass `quality=substantive` to hide idle (0 turns, 0 tokens, and 0 tool uses) sessions, or `quality=idle` to return only those idle sessions. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum sessions to return (1–100).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of sessions to skip.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Column to sort by.

parameters.name: sortDir
parameters.description: Sort direction.

400.description: Invalid query parameters (e.g. `viewerScope=team` with no `teamId`, or `teamId` alongside a non-`team` `viewerScope`).

403.description: The API key lacks the `read` scope, or the requested team scope is not authorized.

get.description: Returns one agent session with its detail-only extensions — per-model token usage, the session's agents, its raw event stream, and per-file transcript availability — on top of every field the list row carries. The read is scoped to the authenticated organization, so a session belonging to another organization returns `404` rather than `403`. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Agent-session UUID (the `id` returned by `GET /agent-sessions`).

403.description: The API key lacks the `read` scope.

404.description: No agent session with that id exists in the authenticated organization.

get.description: Aggregates the organization's agent sessions into a usage summary: session and token totals, the three-way cost split (subscription-covered, confirmed metered, and unclassified spend), and breakdowns by user, model, harness, and repository. Accepts the same filters as `GET /agent-sessions` and covers exactly the population that endpoint lists for the same query, so the totals reconcile against the list. Like the list, the date window is an ACTIVITY window on `lastActivityAt`. Pass `comparison=prior` to also receive server-computed period-over-period movement. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.name: comparison
parameters.description: Opt in to server-computed period-over-period movement, returned in `comparison`. `prior` measures against a window one full period back, so the two slices sit at the same phase of the period — while the requested period is still running that window is cut to the span it has ELAPSED, so the two are equal-length and equal-phase but NOT adjacent (see `AgentSessionUsageComparison`). Requires BOTH `startDate` and `endDate`; with either missing there is no window to step back from and no `comparison` is returned. Accepted only on this endpoint — the list, analytics, and export reads reject it rather than accepting and dropping it.

200.description: The usage summary for the matched sessions.

400.description: Invalid query parameters (e.g. `viewerScope=team` with no `teamId`, or `teamId` alongside a non-`team` `viewerScope`).

403.description: The API key lacks the `read` scope, or the requested team scope is not authorized.

get.description: Breaks the organization's agent sessions down by tool, agent type, repository, and project. Accepts the same filters as `GET /agent-sessions`, with one deliberate difference: the date window here is a session START window on the session's start time, not the list's and usage summary's `lastActivityAt` activity window — so the same `startDate`/`endDate` can match a different set of sessions than the list does. This read has NO server-side population cap, and no `limit` parameter to supply — the query schema is strict, so a caller cannot voluntarily bound the population even if they want to. With no `startDate`/`endDate` it pages every session in the organization into memory, holding two full accumulations of the result at once, and each matched session's event stream is itself fetched unbounded — unlike the single-session detail read, which caps events at 10,000. The failure mode is MEMORY, not latency: a large enough request can exhaust the API process's heap and fail the request outright rather than merely running slowly, and a request timeout does not bound it. Always send a `startDate`/`endDate` window. Requires the `read` scope.

200.description: The analytics breakdowns for the matched sessions.

400.description: Invalid query parameters (e.g. `viewerScope=team` with no `teamId`, or `teamId` alongside a non-`team` `viewerScope`).

403.description: The API key lacks the `read` scope, or the requested team scope is not authorized.

delete.description: Deletes an artifact link by UUID, org-scoped to the authenticated organization. Requires the `delete` scope.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Artifact-link UUID.

403.description: The API key lacks the `delete` scope.

500.description: Failed to delete the artifact link.

bearerAuth.description: Authenticate requests using a Closedloop API key. API keys begin with `sk_live_` and are generated in the Closedloop dashboard. Pass the key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...`

AgentSessionViewerScope.name: viewerScope
AgentSessionViewerScope.description: Read scope. `team` requires `teamId`. The ORGANIZATION is the real data boundary here, not the team: `self` is the only value enforced server-side as a narrowing (the read is pinned to the authenticated user), and the team-membership check runs only when you ASK for team scope. A caller who is 403'd requesting team X can omit `viewerScope` and still receive team X's sessions under the default organization scope. Treat `team` as a view, not a permission.

AgentSessionTeamId.name: teamId
AgentSessionTeamId.description: Team UUID. Required when `viewerScope=team`. Sending `teamId` with NO `viewerScope` is accepted as a legacy alias and normalizes to `viewerScope=team`; sending it alongside any other `viewerScope` is rejected.

AgentSessionStatus.name: status
AgentSessionStatus.description: Filter by a single session status. The canonical filter vocabulary this parameter advertises is `active`, `waiting`, `inactive`, `error`, `stale`, `unknown` — the six values a Status facet offers. The schema stays an open string rather than an enum on purpose: the route matches any spelling it is given, so publishing a narrower contract would make a generated client reject a value the server answers. A spelling outside the six falls through to an exact match on the stored status, so the retired `completed` and `abandoned` are no longer recognized and select nothing rather than joining the `inactive` population. What a row READS BACK is derived rather than stored, and need not be one of the six: a spelling the server does not recognize reads `unknown`, and a stored `active` row reads `waiting` while it awaits input or `stale` once silent past the display cutoff. ISS-5592 retired the last aliases, so `running` and `failed` are no longer recognized either and read `unknown` like any other unmodelled spelling — with the same awaiting-input exception the retired pair carries: that projection runs AHEAD of the unrecognized fold and excludes only spellings the fold reads as terminal, so an unrecognized row carrying an awaiting-input marker and no end time reads `waiting`, not `unknown`. For `failed` that is new: it previously resolved to `error`, which IS terminal and blocked the branch, so a `failed` row that would once have read Error can now read Waiting. These read-back spellings are not themselves selectable by the six values above.

AgentSessionQuality.name: quality
AgentSessionQuality.description: `all` (default) returns every session; `substantive` returns only substantive sessions (at least one turn, token, or tool use); `idle` returns only idle sessions (0 turns, 0 tokens, and 0 tool uses).

AgentSessionActivityStartDate.name: startDate
AgentSessionActivityStartDate.description: Lower bound of the activity window. Keeps only sessions whose `lastActivityAt` falls on or after this date — a point-in-time test on the session's latest activity, not a start-date filter and not an interval overlap. A session with no `lastActivityAt` falls back to `sessionStartedAt`.

AgentSessionActivityEndDate.name: endDate
AgentSessionActivityEndDate.description: Upper bound of the activity window. Keeps only sessions whose `lastActivityAt` falls on or before this date, so a session that was active inside the window but active again after it is excluded. A session with no `lastActivityAt` falls back to `sessionStartedAt`.

AgentSessionStartedStartDate.name: startDate
AgentSessionStartedStartDate.description: Only sessions STARTED on or after this date. Unlike the list and usage reads, analytics windows on the session start time, so a session that started before the window is excluded even if it was active inside it.

AgentSessionStartedEndDate.name: endDate
AgentSessionStartedEndDate.description: Only sessions STARTED on or before this date. Analytics windows on the session start time, not on last activity.

AgentSessionCompletedAfter.name: completedAfter
AgentSessionCompletedAfter.description: Keep only sessions that FINISHED at or after this instant (`sessionEndedAt >= completedAfter`). This is a separate bound from the `startDate`/`endDate` window and composes with it: a session that started before this instant but ended after it is kept. Unlike that window — whose field differs per endpoint — this bound is applied to the session end time on every endpoint that accepts it. A session that is still running has no end time and is therefore always excluded.

AgentSessionStatuses.name: statuses
AgentSessionStatuses.description: Multi-select form of `status`. Repeat the key to select several values (`?statuses=active&statuses=error`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet. This multi-select takes PRECEDENCE over the single-value `status`: when `statuses` is present and non-empty, `status` is ignored outright — it is neither intersected nor unioned with it. So `?status=active&statuses=error` returns every `error` session, not an empty result. Send one or the other, never both. Each item carries the same canonical filter vocabulary — and the same deliberately open string schema — that `status` advertises.

AgentSessionUserIds.name: userIds
AgentSessionUserIds.description: Multi-select form of `userId` — session owners. Repeat the key to select several values (`?userIds=<uuid>&userIds=<uuid>`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet. Intersects with `userId` rather than widening past it: when `userId` is also sent, it wins if it appears in `userIds`, and no sessions are returned if it does not.

AgentSessionRepositories.name: repositories
AgentSessionRepositories.description: Repository full names (`owner/repo`). Repeat the key to select several values (`?repositories=acme/api`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet. Matched against the session's own stored repository. That is not always the `repositoryFullName` response field: the response resolves the repository from the session's touched-branch link first and only falls back to the stored value, so a session whose branch provenance names a different repository is matched here on the stored value while the response reports the branch's.

AgentSessionHarnesses.name: harnesses
AgentSessionHarnesses.description: Multi-select form of `harness`. Repeat the key to select several values (`?harnesses=claude&harnesses=codex`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet. Takes precedence over the single-value `harness`, which stays for backward compatibility.

AgentSessionModels.name: models
AgentSessionModels.description: Matches the session's PRIMARY displayed model — the same value the session record reports as `model`, not every model a session's subagents used. Repeat the key to select several values (`?models=<model>&models=<model>`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet.

AgentSessionAutonomyTiers.name: autonomyTiers
AgentSessionAutonomyTiers.description: Autonomy-tier ids. The canonical ids are `high`, `mixed`, `guided`, and `unknown`; any other id is accepted and then ignored by the server rather than rejected, so no `enum` is published here. Repeat the key to select several values (`?autonomyTiers=high&autonomyTiers=mixed`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet.

AgentSessionCostBuckets.name: costBuckets
AgentSessionCostBuckets.description: Cost-bucket ids. The canonical ids are `under_1` (≤ $1), `from_1_to_10`, `from_10_to_50`, `from_50`, and `unknown` (the session's cost was never computed); any other id is accepted and then ignored by the server rather than rejected, so no `enum` is published here. Buckets match the session's RECONCILED cost, not the stored cost rollup, so a legacy session whose rollup reads 0 still lands in the bucket its priced events total. Repeat the key to select several values (`?costBuckets=under_1`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet.

AgentSessionChangePresence.name: changePresence
AgentSessionChangePresence.description: Whether the session produced file changes. The canonical ids are `has_changes` and `no_changes`; any other id is accepted and then ignored by the server rather than rejected, so no `enum` is published here. Repeat the key to select several values (`?changePresence=has_changes`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet.

AgentSessionPrAssociation.name: prAssociation
AgentSessionPrAssociation.description: Whether the session has an associated pull request. The canonical ids are `has_pr` and `no_pr`; any other id is accepted and then ignored by the server rather than rejected, so no `enum` is published here. Repeat the key to select several values (`?prAssociation=has_pr`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet.

AgentSessionProjectIds.name: projectIds
AgentSessionProjectIds.description: Projects a session TOUCHED — sessions that linked a document belonging to one of these projects. This is a DIFFERENT dimension from `projectId`, not another spelling of it: `projectId` matches the session's own artifact parent, which is null for essentially every desktop-synced session, while `projectIds` walks the session-to-document links. Sending both ANDs them. Repeat the key to select several values (`?projectIds=<uuid>&projectIds=<uuid>`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet.

AgentSessionSearch.name: search
AgentSessionSearch.description: Accepted and then IGNORED. Retained only so already-installed clients that still serialize it are not rejected by validation; there is no server-side search predicate behind it. Sending it does not narrow the result set — do not present it as a filter.

DocumentType.description: The type of document artifact. PRD = Product Requirements Document, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN = implementation plan, TEMPLATE = reusable template, FEATURE = feature specification, DOC = evergreen document.

DocumentTypeInput.description: The accepted document-type input on requests. Supersets the persisted `DocumentType` with the `ISSUE` alias: the product renamed Features to Issues in the UI, so a caller may pass `ISSUE` and it is normalized to the persisted `FEATURE` type. `ISSUE` never persists and never appears in responses (response `type` fields use `DocumentType`), so `type=ISSUE` and `type=FEATURE` both resolve to the same FEATURE-typed artifacts.

IssueStatus.description: The delivery lifecycle status of a Feature (`type=FEATURE`). Distinct from `DocumentStatus`, which applies to the authoring document types (PRD, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN, TEMPLATE, DOC). Omitting `status` on `POST /documents` for a Feature yields `BACKLOG` (the subtype fallback applied by `fallbackStatusForSubtype`), regardless of caller. `TRIAGE` is NOT an omitted-status default: agent workflows land in `TRIAGE` only because they send it explicitly. Every value, including `TRIAGE`, is selectable by any caller.

DocumentListPage.description: Paged list envelope returned by `GET /documents?includeTotal=true` (ISS-4576). The requested page of documents plus a real server-side `total` counted over the same filter, so a paging client can state an honest "showing X-Y of N" without inferring the total from the page length.

items.description: The requested page of documents, in the same order the bare-array response returns.

total.description: Real count of every document matching the filter, counted server-side independently of `limit`/`offset`. Never derived from `items.length`.

limit.description: Effective page size the server applied after clamping, or `null` when the caller requested no bound (the whole matching set is in `items`).

offset.description: Effective zero-based offset the server applied after clamping.

hasMore.description: True when documents matching the filter exist beyond this page.

status.description: Status of the document. Uses the Documents or Features vocabulary depending on `type`.

query.description: The search query that was executed. Empty string for tag-scoped searches.

documents.description: Matching documents, capped at 25 (the same cap applies to a `?tagId=` search). This shape carries no `hasMore`, `nextCursor`, or `offset`, so a caller that receives 25 cannot tell whether more matched — use the unified path and its `nextCursor` to page the full corpus.

projects.description: Matching projects, capped at 25 independently of `documents`. As with `documents`, this shape carries no continuation metadata — page via the unified path.

tagId.description: Present when the search was scoped to a tag via `?tagId=`.

tagName.description: Name of the scoped tag, when `tagId` is set.

SearchMode.description: Query mode for the unified search path. `fulltext` (the default) is phrase/operator-aware; `prefix` is typeahead — the trailing token matches as a prefix so a partially-typed word still hits.

SearchEntityType.description:
One entity kind in the unified-search corpus. Also the accepted vocabulary for the `types` query param — a value outside this set is rejected with a 400, never silently dropped.

`agent_session` is accepted for every organization but only *matches* for one that has opted into transcript search: session transcripts are privacy-sensitive, so an opted-out org gets an empty session result rather than an error.

SearchHit.description: One heterogeneous, ranked hit in a `UnifiedSearchResponse`. `entityType` discriminates the kind; the route fields are optional because a hit that lacks the data to build an in-app route degrades to a non-link row rather than a broken one.

snippet.description: Highlighted excerpt around the match, or a plain title fallback.

rank.description: Relevance score; higher is more relevant.

updatedAt.description: The source entity's own last-updated timestamp.

deepLink.description: Org-relative UUID-only locator (e.g. `/documents/<id>`). Best-effort: prefer building the route from the fields below, which resolve the real app path.

slug.description: The entity's URL handle, when it has one (documents route by slug; agent components by their `${kind}::${key}` handle).

entitySubtype.description: A document hit's `type` (used to pick the route prefix), or — for a comment hit — the TYPE of the artifact it is anchored on.

teamId.description: A project hit's owning team, for the team-scoped project route.

anchorEntityId.description: The id of a DIFFERENT entity this hit routes to: a `pull_request` routes to its owning branch, a `comment` to the artifact it is anchored on.

UnifiedSearchResponse.description: The unified full-text search response — a heterogeneous ranked list across the whole corpus. Returned INSTEAD of `GlobalSearchResponse` whenever the request takes the unified path (see the `GET /search` description).

query.description: The free-text portion of the query that was executed, with any inline filter tokens removed. The first bare token that resolves as an entity UUID or slug is also lifted out — into the exact-lookup lane — so it does not appear here either (`?q=FEA-42 auth` echoes `auth`). Empty when no free text remained: the query was all filters, or only that exact ID/slug token (`?q=FEA-42` echoes `""`).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page — pass it back as `cursor`. `null` when the result set is drained.

AgentSessionListItem.description: One agent session row. This documents the stable core fields; the endpoint also returns many optional, additive projection fields (git diff stats, phases, activity buckets, linked PRs/artifacts, …) that a client should treat as best-effort.

slug.description: SES-* slug of the backing Session artifact.

status.description: Status of the session, DERIVED at read time rather than served from the stored column — so it is NOT bounded by the canonical filter vocabulary the `status`/`statuses` parameters advertise, whose request schemas stay open strings for version-skewed clients. A stored `active` can come back as `waiting` (awaiting user input on a run that has not ended) or as `stale` (silent past the display staleness cutoff), and a stored value this build does not recognize generally comes back as `unknown` — the awaiting-input derivation runs first, so even an unrecognized row can surface as `waiting`. Where no derivation applies the stored value passes through unchanged, including a retired `completed`/`abandoned` from a not-yet-migrated row. Treat this as an open string rather than a closed vocabulary, and do not assume re-sending a returned value as a filter finds the row that carried it.

harness.description: The agent harness that produced the session (e.g. `claude`, `codex`).

cwd.description: Working directory the session ran in.

repositoryFullName.description: The `owner/repo` the session worked in, if known.

model.description: Primary model used by the session.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the session row was last updated.

lastActivityAt.description: Timestamp of the latest genuine agent activity (the default Sessions sort).

endedAt.description: Timestamp when the session ended, if it has.

estimatedCost.description: Estimated cost of the session in USD.

agentCount.description: Number of distinct agents in the session.

toolUseCount.description: Number of tool calls in the session.

errorCount.description: Number of errors recorded in the session.

baseBranch.description: The base branch the session's work targeted.

sourceArtifactId.description: ID of the artifact that sourced the session, if any.

sourceLoopId.description: ID of the loop that produced the session, if any.

user.description: The user who owns the session. Null when the owner has been deleted.

computeTarget.description: Summary of the compute target that produced the session.

project.description: Summary of the project the session is associated with, if any.

total.description: Total number of sessions matching the filters.

viewerScope.description: The scope the results were read at.

idleCount.description: Number of idle sessions hidden by the `quality=substantive` view (the default `quality=all` view returns every session). Omitted (treated as 0) by producers that do not compute it.

AgentSessionAgent.description: One agent (main or subagent) that ran inside the session.

id.description: Stable persisted agent-row identity, when the producer exposes it.

type.description: Agent type as reported by the harness.

subagentType.description: Subagent type, for a spawned subagent.

task.description: The task the agent was given.

currentTool.description: Tool the agent was last using.

awaitingInputSince.description: When the agent began waiting on user input, if it is.

parentExternalAgentId.description: The spawning agent's identifier, for a subagent.

AgentSessionEvent.description: One recorded event in the session's stream. Turn and tool TEXT is not part of the cloud lane — read the archived transcript for that.

agentExternalId.description: The agent that produced the event.

toolName.description: Tool involved in the event, for tool events.

AgentSessionTokenUsage.description: Token usage for ONE model the session used — the primary model plus any secondary/subagent model.

cacheWrite5mTokens.description: 5-minute ephemeral prompt-cache writes. Omitted or null means the provider never reported a TTL breakdown — never read it as zero.

cacheWrite1hTokens.description: 1-hour ephemeral prompt-cache writes. Omitted or null means the provider never reported a TTL breakdown — never read it as zero.

estimatedCostUsd.description: Estimated cost attributed to this model, in USD.

AgentSessionAttribution.description: Where the session's work was attributed — the repository, worktree, and originating artifact/loop it was associated with.

AgentSessionTranscriptAvailability.description: Availability of ONE archived transcript file (the main run or a subagent sidechain). Reading the file itself needs a separate signed-URL request.

fileKey.description: Identifies which transcript file this entry describes.

availability.description: `permanentlyUnavailable` is terminal — no retry can recover the file — unlike the retryable `uploadFailed`.

uploadedAt.description: When the file was archived, or null if it has not been.

permanentFailureReason.description: Why a `permanentlyUnavailable` file was terminally skipped (e.g. `too_large`); null for every other availability state.

AgentSessionDetail.description: One agent session with its detail-only extensions on top of every field a list row carries. Like `AgentSessionListItem` this documents the stable core; the endpoint also returns optional, additive projection fields (derived timeline and turn items, activity segments, trace sources, …) that a client should treat as best-effort.

metadata.description: Free-form harness metadata captured with the session.

tokenUsageByModel.description: Per-model token and cost breakdown across every model the session used.

attribution.description: Repository/worktree/origin attribution, or null when none was captured.

agents.description: The agents that ran inside the session.

events.description: The session's event stream, oldest first. May be a partial prefix — see `eventsTruncated`.

eventsTruncated.description: Present and `true` only when `events` is an intentionally partial, chronological PREFIX because the stored stream exceeded the read's row ceiling. ABSENCE is the only encoding of "complete" — the field is never serialized as `false` — so a client must not present a truncated trace as the whole run.

transcripts.description: Per-file transcript availability: the main transcript plus one entry per subagent file.

AgentSessionUsageByUser.description: Usage totals for the sessions owned by one user.

AgentSessionUsageByModel.description: Usage totals grouped by EVERY model a session used — the primary model plus any secondary/subagent model. This is a cost-attribution lens, so it deliberately does not match the single primary model reported as a session's `model`.

AgentSessionHarnessBreakdown.description: Usage totals for the sessions produced by one agent harness.

AgentSessionRepositoryBreakdown.description: Usage totals for the sessions that worked in one repository.

AgentSessionProjectBreakdown.description: Usage totals for one project, under the ANALYTICS definition of project membership: the session's OWN artifact is parented to that project. A session whose artifact has no project contributes no row, and there is deliberately no inferred repository-to-project fallback. A desktop-synced session is parented ONLY when its reported attribution carries a `sourceArtifactId` or `sourceLoopId` that resolves to a project; absent that its artifact is created unparented, so essentially every desktop-synced session is missing here — but not literally every one, and this is not a guarantee to code against. This is a DIFFERENT dimension from the `projectIds` filter and from the usage summary's project facet, which instead count the sessions that LINKED a document belonging to a project; the same session can be present under one and absent under the other, so do not reconcile these counts against those.

AgentSessionToolBreakdown.description: How often one tool was invoked across the matched sessions.

sessionCount.description: How many distinct sessions used the tool.

AgentSessionAgentTypeBreakdown.description: How one agent type performed across the matched sessions.

avgDurationMs.description: Mean duration in milliseconds, or null when no agent of this type has a measurable duration.

AgentSessionLastSyncTarget.description: Sync freshness for one of the organization's compute targets. This list is NOT drawn from the session population the rest of the summary describes: it is every non-sentinel compute target in the organization, narrowed only by `userId` and `teamId` when those are set, and never tested against the date window, `quality`, or any other active filter. A target that contributed no session to these totals still appears, and a target's presence here is not evidence it is represented above. The list is also capped at the 20 most recently synced targets, ranked by the last sync ATTEMPT rather than by when data last landed, so on a larger fleet treat it as a freshness affordance and not a complete inventory.

lastAgentSessionSyncAt.description: When session rows from this target last LANDED in the cloud. An accepted sync that carried nothing new does not advance it, so read it as landed-data freshness and use `lastAgentSessionSyncAttemptAt` for "did it sync". Null until the target's first rows land.

lastAgentSessionSyncAttemptAt.description: When a batch from this target was last accepted, INCLUDING a batch carrying no new sessions — the honest "last successful sync". Null until the first accepted batch.

AgentSessionUsageComparison.description: Period-over-period movement, returned only when the caller passes `comparison=prior` and a prior window exists.

priorStartDate.description: Start of the prior window the deltas were measured against — one full period before the current window opens.

priorEndDate.description: End of that window. While the current period is still running this is cut to the span the current window has elapsed, so the two are equal-length and equal-phase but not adjacent.

deltas.description: Signed percent movement per compared metric. A key is present only when an honest comparison exists — an ABSENT key is the wire form of "no comparison" (no prior window, a prior base too near zero to divide by, or a magnitude past the display ceiling), never a zero.

AgentSessionUsageSummary.description:
Aggregated usage for the sessions matching the query. This documents the stable core; the endpoint also returns optional, additive lenses (per-branch and per-PR splits, and the filter-facet option lists) that a client should treat as best-effort.

TWO DIFFERENT POPULATIONS live in this object, and they are not meant to reconcile. The TOTALS (`totalSessions`, the token totals, and the cost split) describe the fully filtered population — exactly the sessions the list returns for the same query. The `byUser`, `byHarness`, and `byRepository` breakdowns are FACET-OPTION populations: each is computed with its OWN dimension's selection removed, so the reader can still see the options they could widen to instead of a list collapsed to the one value already selected. With `harness=claude` active, `totalSessions` counts Claude sessions only while `byHarness` still reports every harness, and summing a facet's rows will exceed the totals. Present these as filter options, never as a decomposition of the headline numbers.

viewerScope.description: The scope the aggregate was read at.

totalSessions.description: Number of sessions matching the filters — the fully filtered population, the same one `GET /agent-sessions` lists for this query.

earliestSessionAt.description: Earliest session start across matching sessions, or null when none match. With `latestSessionAt`, describes the span the totals cover.

latestSessionAt.description: Latest session start across matching sessions, or null when none match.

totalEstimatedCost.description: Subscription-INCLUSIVE grand total, equal to `subscriptionEstimatedCost + apiEstimatedCost` by construction.

subscriptionEstimatedCost.description: Spend on subscription-covered compute targets — priced only as a hypothetical "would have cost", not money billed.

apiEstimatedCost.description: Everything NOT covered by a subscription — `meteredEstimatedCost + unknownEstimatedCost`.

meteredEstimatedCost.description: The CONFIRMED-metered half of `apiEstimatedCost` — the only figure that may be presented as money actually spent. An absent value means the producer cannot split the bucket, never that nothing was billed.

unknownEstimatedCost.description: The half of `apiEstimatedCost` whose billing mode was never determined — neither confirmed metered nor confirmed subscription. Disclose it rather than folding it into a headline as definite cost. The three figures are summed independently, so reconcile with a tolerance rather than exact equality.

mergedPrCount.description: Merged PRs in the selected range. The three delivery figures below do NOT share the session cohort the totals use: their scope keeps every facet filter but DROPS `startDate`/`endDate`, and the selected range is then applied to each pull request's own `mergedAt`. So a session that fell outside the activity window still contributes a PR that merged inside it — deliberately, since bounding on session activity could only understate what shipped in the range. Null means there were none to count (no data — never a fabricated 0); absent means this surface does not compute it.

medianPrSize.description: Median gross lines (additions + deletions) across merged PRs — the same `mergedAt`-bounded, session-date-unbounded SCOPE as `mergedPrCount`, but measured over a strict SUBSET of it: only PRs whose per-PR line-diff enrichment has already run are included, since an un-enriched row carries no line counts and would drag the median down with a placeholder 0. A PR that `mergedPrCount` counts can therefore be absent from this median, so do not reconcile the two. Null when there are no enriched merged PRs to measure.

mergedLocPerDollar.description: Merged gross LINES divided by API-billed cost — LOC per dollar, higher is better. READ THE TWO SIDES CAREFULLY: the numerator is bounded by the selected range at each PR's `mergedAt`, but the denominator is the API spend of the whole date-unbounded delivery scope, so narrowing the date range moves the numerator while the denominator stays put. It is not the ratio of lines to cost within the window, and it is not comparable across two different ranges. Subscription-covered spend is excluded from the denominator. Null when there are no merged lines to count or no cost to divide by.

mergedKlocPerDollar.description: Deprecated KLOC-unit predecessor of `mergedLocPerDollar` (LOC/$ divided by 1000), retained only for already-installed clients. Read `mergedLocPerDollar` instead — never render this directly.

byUser.description: Owner FACET-OPTION population: computed with the `userIds` selection removed, so it lists every owner available to widen to. ONLY `userIds` is removed — unlike the harness facet, which drops both of its params, the single-value `userId` and `viewerScope=self` are treated as caller-supplied scope and deliberately SURVIVE the exclusion. A request carrying either therefore gets a breakdown collapsed to that one owner, not the org-wide option list. Does not sum to `totalSessions` when an owner filter is active. Owners that cannot be resolved are dropped.

byModel.description: Cost lens by model over the FULLY FILTERED population — unlike the facet-option breakdowns above, this one honours every active filter. It spans every model a matched session used, including subagent models, so a single session can appear under several models and these counts still will not sum to `totalSessions`.

byHarness.description: Harness FACET-OPTION population: computed with the `harness`/`harnesses` selection removed, so it lists every harness available to widen to. Does not sum to `totalSessions` when a harness filter is active.

byRepository.description: Repository FACET-OPTION population: computed with the `repositories` selection removed, so it lists every repository available to widen to. Does not sum to `totalSessions` when a repository filter is active. Sessions with no captured repository are dropped.

lastSyncTargets.description: Sync freshness per compute target, capped at 20. An organization-scoped list that does not follow the query's filters — see `AgentSessionLastSyncTarget`.

AgentSessionAnalytics.description: Breakdowns across the sessions matching the query. This documents the stable core; the endpoint also returns optional, additive lenses (per-branch and per-PR splits) that a client should treat as best-effort.

viewerScope.description: The scope the breakdowns were read at.
